data.narrative:
Cellares, a Series C biotech company founded by Fabian Gerlinghaus and Omar Kurdi, has raised $350M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 3 public-market peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and New Limit at similar stage and sector.

Two methods triangulate the valuation. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C-to-next advancement, anchoring to a $12M total-raised proxy, yielding $20.4M. Peer-median methodology directly compares Cellares to 3 same-sector, same-stage private companies with a median valuation of $3.8B (range $3.1B–$10.3B). Public-comp anchoring, though methodologically sound given a sector P/S median of 6.6x, cannot be applied; Cellares' revenue is not disclosed, limiting the applicability of this method.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.9B (median), bounded by $17.3M at the low end and $4.4B at the high end. The wide dispersion—particularly the $10.3B outlier from Colossal Biosciences—reflects heterogeneity in frontier-biotech advancement and funding environments. Key uncertainty centers on Cellares' commercial traction and pipeline advancement relative to its peer set, data not available in this dataset.
